audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side read 'Skill' while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Fizz/Fizz/Skill/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz/Akali. The page rendered a flat seven-way coinflip against its own content layer. Akali was also called 'he/his/him' in 19 fields.
audit.why: Fizz has the level 1-2 edge because Twilight Shroud is not levelled and Akali's Five Point Strike costs 110 energy at rank 1; level 3 is genuinely even once Shroud is up; 4-6 return to Fizz as Playful/Trickster's grounding answers her Shuriken Flip recast and Chum the Waters punishes the Shroud exit; two items onward Akali pulls ahead on a 16s Shroud plus an execute ultimate.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides moved onto the content values, whys rewritten in the same proposal to match each verdict. All 19 misgender findings fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes and phases[5].why claimed the string 'one-shots squishies' with no source, and spikes[3].text named 'Twin Disciplines' as Akali's passive.
audit.why: Akali's passive in the kit file is Assassin's Mark — an energy ring that empowers her next attack with bonus range and damage. Twin Disciplines does not exist in this kit. No damage magnitudes appear in either champion's text.
audit.corrected: Fabricated passive name removed and the late spike restated on the real late threat: Perfect Execution's execute threshold (120/90/60 cooldown). Magnitude claims replaced with mechanics.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chum the Waters was described as ROOTING Akali out of Shroud in three places (spikes[1].text, content.mid, whys[3]). It does not root. The page also never mentioned the single most decisive interaction in this lane: Playful/Trickster grounds.
audit.why: Fizz's R text: it slows the target, then 'knocking up the target' — a slow followed by a knockup, plus the revealsStealth flag. Fizz's E carries the grounding flag ('shuts off enemy dashes'), and Akali's E is explicitly a recast DASH to the marked target and her R is two dashes. Grounding her recast is what strands her on top of you, and nothing on the page said so.
audit.corrected: R restated as reveals-stealth plus slow-then-knockup on the Shroud exit. Added the grounding interaction to phases[3].why, dosFull[1].d, breakdown.cooldowns and content.mid. Added the execute-threshold warning from missingInteractions to spikes[3].text, breakdown.late and content.late.
sources: ownerKit R text and revealsStealth flag
enemyKit E text ('Re-cast to dash to the marked target')

audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20/19/18/17/16, Shuriken Flip 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, Perfect Execution 120/90/60, Five Point Strike a flat 1.5s gated by energy.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in, with the step-up window keyed to Shroud's cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).

edits.before: Late game is where Akali claws it back — with Shroud on a low cooldown and a full combo of Q resets, she can burst backline targets from stealth almost instantly, and if your dodge timing on her E flip is off by even a second you eat the full combo. Build some early defensive utility and always hold your E for her engage rather than for repositioning, since a missed dodge here is often a death.
edits.after: Late game is where Akali claws it back — with Shroud down to 16s and Five Point Strike on a 1.5s cooldown she can burst backline targets out of stealth, and Perfect Execution finishes anyone under its threshold, so a dodge that is a second late is a death. Build defensive utility, watch that HP number, and hold your E for her engage rather than for repositioning.

CHART: the full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] matched packet.levelChart exactly (Fizz/Fizz/Skill/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz/Akali). The FULL layer was the wrong one, so the side edits move it onto the content values and carry no paired win[N] edit — win[N] is already correct on disk and an edit there would be a no-op the applier rejects. SuspectName 'Seastone Trident' in spikes[0].text is a FALSE POSITIVE — it is Fizz's real W. The genuine name error was elsewhere: spikes[3].text invented 'Twin Disciplines' as Akali's passive when the kit's passive is Assassin's Mark.

UNVERIFIED / QUESTION FOR THE USER, deliberately NOT written to the page: whether Chum the Waters can attach to Akali while she is inside Twilight Shroud. Her W says she is 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks'; Fizz's R says the fish 'attaches to any champion that touches it' and carries revealsStealth. Riot's text does not settle whether a contact-attach skillshot bypasses the unselectable state. I wrote only the part I can source — that R reveals stealth and punishes her on the EXIT — and avoided claiming it lands on her inside the smoke.
